home_title: Cicada: live subtitles, interpreting and meeting notes for any call or stream | Free for Mac, Windows, Linux and Android
home_desc: Cicada listens to whatever your computer or phone is playing and gives you live translated subtitles, push-to-talk interpreting and AI meeting notes. Works in Zoom, Teams, Google Meet, X Spaces, YouTube Live and Discord, with no bot in the call. For Mac, Windows, Linux and Android, free and open source; on the Mac, audio never leaves your computer.

faq: Will it run on my Mac?

You need macOS 14.4 or later on an Apple silicon Mac. macOS 26 uses the newer on-device speech recognizer, the most accurate; 14.4 to 15 use the system's earlier one, a little weaker, which needs Dictation turned on in System Settings › Keyboard, with each language you want heard added to it.
What about Windows, Linux and phones?

Windows 10 (2004) or later, the Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04 desktop and Android 10 or later are all supported, with the same meeting records as the Mac. These apps recognize speech with Ming, so they need a Ling key. On Linux the notes window shows up in screen sharing; on Android, interpreting is face to face through the speaker. The iPhone app is on its way.

Cicada is free and open source. On the Mac, live subtitles, translation and meeting records work without a key; AI notes and natural voices use your own Ling key, about ¥0.15–1 per hour of meeting. The Windows, Linux and Android apps need a key. Ling gives ¥10 of credit every month.
No bot joins the call, and nobody else installs anything. When you share your screen on Mac, Windows or Android, the notes window stays out of the picture by default.

On the Mac, audio turns into text on your computer; only the recognized text leaves it, plus the few sentences you say while holding the talk key for interpreting. The Windows, Linux and Android apps recognize speech with Ming, so what is said is sent to Ling in short pieces. Recordings stay on your own device.

On the Mac, any language its on-device speech recognition supports is detected; on the other platforms Ming recognizes it. Translations go into your system language by default. Natural interpreting voices cover English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, German, French and Spanish.
Is what I say out loud recorded?
For now, only what you say while holding the talk key. “Record what I say” is first on the roadmap.

Cicada isn’t notarized by Apple or code-signed for Windows yet. On a Mac, go to System Settings › Privacy & Security and click “Open Anyway”; on Windows, click “More info › Run anyway”. Only once. Proper signing is on the roadmap.

On the Mac, a virtual microphone, BlackHole: the first time you turn on interpreting, Cicada downloads it from the official source and installs it. On Windows, the free VB-Cable, which the guide helps you install. On Linux nothing: Cicada makes its own “Cicada Microphone”.

a_s1_p: Download the APK on your phone and open it to install.
a_gate_p: Tap Settings in the prompt and allow installs for the app you downloaded it with (your browser or a chat app).
a_gate_note: The wording and place differ by brand; follow the system’s prompt.
a_s3_h: Open Cicada and follow the guide
a_s3_li2: What Cicada listens to: the phone’s own sound (videos, streams, classes) or In person (in the room, or a call on speaker)
a_s3_li3: Allow the microphone, notifications and “Display over other apps”
a_s3_aside_h: “Display over other apps” is where people get stuck
a_s3_aside_p: It depends on your Android version and brand; see your phone below.
a_s3_note: Cicada’s guide works out which case you’re in and takes you through it.
a_guide_p: Each brand and Android version stops you in a different place. Find yours.
a_ov1_p: Tap Turn on in the guide, find Cicada in the list and turn on “Display over other apps”. It’s only used for the subtitle card.
a_ov2_h: The system blocks the switch first
a_ov2_p: Apps installed from a browser or chat app must be unlocked once: tap the switch and get refused, then in App info choose ⋮ › Allow restricted settings, confirm with your screen lock and go back to turn it on.
a_ov3_p: Tap Open permission settings in the guide; under Other permissions, allow “Display pop-up windows” and “Display pop-up windows while running in the background”. If it says restricted settings, unlock as above first.
a_cap_h: The system asks about screen recording
a_cap_p: Android only lets apps read the phone’s sound through the screen-recording permission. Tap Start: Cicada takes the sound, never the picture.
a_meet_h: No subtitles in WeChat calls, Tencent Meeting or Zoom?
a_meet_p: The system doesn’t let apps record those apps’ sound. Put the call on speaker and switch Cicada to In person, which listens through the microphone. Cicada suggests this after 20 seconds without sound.
